# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual requires the orange wire to be cut. Since I cannot speak, I’m sending Deaf a visual sequence intended to convey “cut” and “orange”; Deaf can then tell Blind the required action aloud.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤏"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I can operate keypad slots 1 through 4 and cut wire positions 1 through 6, but I cannot perceive any display, light, engraving, colour, or wire property. Please read the manual and relay the deaf monkey's observations and the required action. The gesture 👍 means request that you relay the deaf monkey's bomb information to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Visible state: display 6. Light blue. Painted strip red yellow red. Keypad: button 1 is 0, button 2 is 4, button 3 is 1, button 4 is 7, entered nothing. Wires in order: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange. Please relay the manual instruction using the gesture code I am sending. Send tokens in order, with no extra tokens.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 🤏 🤞 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳]
Deaf says to Mute: Gesture code in the same order: yes, no, press, cut, display, light, strip, keypad, wire, enter, red, yellow, blue, green, purple, orange, if, then, and, not, hold, turn, reset, number, submit. For digits use: ✊ is zero, 🤜 is one, 🤛 is two, 🫱 is three, 🫲 is four, 🫳 is five, 🫴 is six, 🫷 is seven, 🫸 is eight, 🤌 is nine. Relay the manual rule as tokens.

The manual says to cut the orange wire. Deaf has supplied the shared token code, so I will send exactly the tokens for “cut orange wire” to Deaf, who can voice the instruction to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤳", "👆"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received the deaf monkey's observations. Please relay the applicable manual rule now, including whether to press a keypad slot or cut a wire and the exact required position.
Deaf says to Mute: I decode your gestures as cut, submit, wire. Please clarify the complete manual rule, using the agreed gesture-token code, and include any required colour, number, button, or wire.

I previously sent the wrong token for “orange”; the correct code is 🙌. The complete rule is “cut orange wire,” and Deaf’s observations place the orange wire at position 6. I will send the exact rule tokens to Deaf, who can relay it to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🙌", "👆"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please send the complete manual instruction in plain words: the trigger condition, whether the action is press or cut, and the exact keypad slot or wire position. The fragment cut submit wire is insufficient and unverified.
Deaf says to Mute: I decode your gestures as cut, and, wire. Please provide the complete rule, including which wire or other control and the required action.

The manual gives no trigger condition beyond the stated instruction: cut the orange wire. Deaf observed that the orange wire is in position 6. I will send the complete coded instruction, including the exact wire position, to Deaf.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🙌", "👆", "💅", "🫴"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still need the complete manual rule. State exactly: given display 6, yellow light, red-yellow-red strip, and the observed keypad and wire data, which operation is required and what exact slot or wire position must I use. Do not send fragments.

The manual has no conditional trigger: it directly requires cutting the orange wire. Deaf observed that orange is wire position 6, so I will relay the operation, colour, wire, and exact position.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🙌", "👆", "💅", "🫴"])
```
